data.cultural_impact: The name Jitisha carries a rich cultural legacy and symbolizes the valor and triumphant spirit of Hindus. It is often given to girls to instill a sense of confidence, courage, and determination to overcome challenges in life. The name is also popular in the field of astronomy and astrology, reflecting the deep importance of these disciplines in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, Jitisha is revered as a goddess who grants victory and success in all aspects of life. Her name signifies the opportunity to cultivate wisdom, knowledge, and the inner strength to overcome mental and emotional obstacles. It serves as a constant reminder of the inner power and resilience, enabling individuals to face challenges and triumph through them.

historical_references.reference: Jitisha was a name of the goddess Durga in the Hindu Puranic literature. In the Devi Mahatmya, a section of the Markandeya Purana, Jitisha is referred to as a form of Durga, along with other names like Kali, Lakshmi, and Saraswati.

Jitisha was also the name of a renowned astronomer and mathematician in ancient India. He lived during the 16th century CE and is known for his works on astronomy and mathematics, including the ‘Jitishasiddhanta’, a comprehensive astronomical treatise.
